reasoning: This is a standard AUR -bin package that downloads prebuilt binaries from the official sqldef/sqldef GitHub repository with pinned versions and SHA-256 checksums. The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments and install commands with no command substitutions, eval, or dynamic code execution. All models that successfully analyzed the PKGBUILD found it safe. The 'inconclusive' results from two models were due to tool errors (HTTP 400 API failures and parse errors), not security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool errors, not substantive security analysis differences. qwen3-235b failed with HTTP 400 errors on .SRCINFO and .nvchecker.toml. openrouter/free failed to parse a decision from .SRCINFO. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. The PKGBUILD (the critical executable file) was successfully analyzed by all three models and unanimously found safe.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b: HTTP 400 errors prevented review of .SRCINFO and .nvchecker.toml
openrouter/free: Failed to parse model response for .SRCINFO
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parse errors) should not cause 'inconclusive' verdicts when critical executable files like PKGBUILD are successfully analyzed and found safe
The audit tool should implement retry logic for failed API calls or gracefully degrade by weighting successfully-analyzed files more heavily
Metadata files (.SRCINFO, .nvchecker.toml, REUSE.toml) should be weighted less heavily than executable files (PKGBUILD, .install hooks) when determining overall package safety
Distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool error' and 'inconclusive due to genuine security uncertainty' in verdict reporting
